coordinates.note: Decimal conversion of the CMS paper's 46 deg 18.57 min N / 6 deg 4.62 min E (46.3095 N, 6.077 E), which refer to the centre of the detector. The quote is the PDF text extraction, in which the degree sign appears as a circle and the minute mark as a trailing 0 (18.570 is 18.57 minutes). precision_m 30 reflects the 0.01 minute rounding of the published values (~18 m in latitude), not a survey uncertainty. The CMS collaboration's own detector page independently places the detector in an underground cavern near Cessy, France.
coordinates.quote: The CMS detector is installed in an underground cavern, with the center of the detector 89 m below Earth’s surface, and 420 m above sea level. The location is 46◦ 18.570 north latitude and 6◦ 4.620 east longitude.

depth.note: Depth of the centre of the detector below the surface, per the CMS atmospheric-muon paper. CMS's own pages describe the cavern as '100 m underground'; see worklog conflict C3.
depth.quote: The CMS detector is installed in an underground cavern, with the center of the detector 89 m below Earth’s surface, and 420 m above sea level.

name: LHC Point 5 — CMS cavern, Cessy
notes: The experiment cavern (UXC55) is quoted by CMS as 53 m long, 27 m wide and 24 m high, 100 m underground; the detector centre is 89 m below the surface and 420 m above sea level.
Altitude is left null: the only sourced altitude (420 m a.s.l.) is that of the detector centre underground, not of the surface site.

summary.plain: The place where the CMS experiment sits: a cavern about 100 metres below the village of Cessy in France, on the ring of the Large Hadron Collider just across the border from Geneva.
summary.technical: Interaction Point 5 of the LHC, near Cessy (Ain, France). The CMS experiment cavern UXC55 is about 100 m below the surface; the detector centre is 89 m below ground and 420 m above sea level, under roughly 50 m of moraine and 20 m of molasse.
